Add a level, nested in the one before it if there is one

Source: R/levels.R
add_level.Rd

The first add_level() in a fabricate() call creates N rows, since there is nothing above it to nest in. A later one nests: it creates N rows inside each row of the level before it, exactly as nest_level does, and the two can be used interchangeably there. For independent (non-nested) levels used in cross_levels or link_levels, use declare_level.

Usage

add_level(N, ...)

Arguments

N

Number of rows to create.

...

Column expressions evaluated sequentially. N is available as a scalar integer.

Value

A fabricatr_level object, meaningful only as a named argument to fabricate. It contributes N rows, an ID column named after the argument it is assigned to, and one column per expression in .... Any level nested below it repeats these rows.

Examples

fabricate(
  villages = add_level(N = 20, income = rnorm(N)),
  citizens = nest_level(N = 5, Y = income + rnorm(N))
)
#> # A tibble: 100 × 4
#>    villages income citizens        Y
#>    <chr>     <dbl> <chr>       <dbl>
#>  1 01       -1.63  001      -0.00744
#>  2 01       -1.63  002      -1.52   
#>  3 01       -1.63  003      -1.76   
#>  4 01       -1.63  004      -3.54   
#>  5 01       -1.63  005      -1.91   
#>  6 02        0.512 006       0.199  
#>  7 02        0.512 007       1.58   
#>  8 02        0.512 008       0.582  
#>  9 02        0.512 009      -0.127  
#> 10 02        0.512 010       0.462  
#> # ℹ 90 more rows
